1.explanation: 1. BreadcrumbItem.js contains the conditional logic that looks for children.type.displayName === 'OverflowMenu' to add the shark-fin icon and position offsets. 2. Breadcrumb.js shows how BreadcrumbItem is rendered in the context of the whole breadcrumb component. 3. OverflowMenu.mdx (and its source) document the API surface of the OverflowMenu component, explaining its default displayName and how it should integrate with BreadcrumbItem. 4. FeatureFlags.js (where createComponentToggle lives) reveals how toggling wraps OverflowMenu in a ComponentToggle without forwarding the original displayName, which is the root cause. 5. Breadcrumb/Breadcrumb.mdx provides the expected behavior and visual examples of overflow handling. 6. OverflowMenu/OverflowMenu.mdx demonstrates the menu’s built-in icon usage and default positioning, confirming how BreadcrumbItem should leverage it. Together these files allow you to see the mismatch in displayName and how to reproduce or patch the issue.
1.bug_scenario: In the reported screenshots we can see a Breadcrumb using an overflow menu: when the number of BreadcrumbItems exceeds the available horizontal space, the overflow item should display a little “shark-fin” arrow (Chevron) and an x/y offset so the menu is positioned correctly. Instead, no shark-fin is rendered and the offset is ignored. Debugging shows that BreadcrumbItem’s code checks children.type.displayName === 'OverflowMenu' before decorating the overflow trigger, but because the OverflowMenu has been wrapped by createComponentToggle, its displayName ends up something like FeatureToggle(OverflowMenu) (and the unwrapped ComponentToggle has no displayName set at all). The mismatch prevents the shark-fin icon and positioning props from ever being applied.
